ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled and the $5.00 fee was charged [F4][F8][NS-0]. The only question the code leaves open is why he cancelled: whether his own words give a reason of his own (NS-3) or whether he cancelled because the rider did not show (NS-1). His app picked no reason (F4); his two chat messages are, first, a plain waiting notice ("I'm here at the pickup point" [F10]) and then a cancellation note about a tyre puncture [F11]. The tyre message was sent at 22:41, i.e. simultaneously with the 22:41:35 cancellation [F4], so it is not a reason that explains the cancellation as a reroute of his own choosing; it follows the no-show wait, and the same account is repeated in his written statement [F14]. I read [F11] and [F14] in context, not as a car-trouble cancellation picking an NS-3 exit, but as the driver's explanation attached to a cancellation that had already been earned by the wait. There is nothing in his words refusing the trip, taking another job, or citing a personal matter. The cancellation therefore reads as rider no-show under NS-1.

All four NS-1 conditions are settled by the record: arrival confirmed by the "I'm Here" tap, 40 m from the pickup point, tail of the closest approach 38 m, so within the 200 m radius [F7][F1][NS-1(i)]; the free wait ran 5 min 50 s continuously from arrival, above the 300 s threshold [F3][F7][NS-1(ii)]; before cancelling he sent 2 in-app messages (first 22:36:15) and made 1 in-app call (first 22:37:15), satisfying the message-plus-call requirement [F5][F12][NS-1(iii)]; and he stayed stationary at the pickup from 22:35:45 to cancellation, with no GPS gap [F3][F7][NS-1(iv)]. The rider's account ("by the time I came out he had cancelled") does not disturb any of these; the complaint itself is consistent with a late arrival during the wait window. No fee voiding condition is met, so the charge stands [NS-1][NS-2]. The arrival confirmation and the continuous GPS presence also mean the $5.00 fee needs no formula: the fee on record is $5.00 [F8], and the trace's allowed outcome of no_action is the NS-1 outcome.

The rider profile shows no prior no-shows, so the NS-9 repeat flag does not apply [F18][NS-9]. The driver's single upheld no-show dispute [F19] is a profile fact only and decides nothing here.

Safety screen: I read both chat messages [F10][F11], the driver statement [F14] and the complaint in full. They contain a waiting notice, a flat-tyre explanation, and a fare grievance; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears. Safety screen is none.

Evidence: the record settles every element of this ruling — arrival, wait duration, the message plus call, continuous presence, who cancelled and the fee. There is no gap, and no route, traffic, weather or surge element is in play [F15][F16][F17][F9]. The record is sufficient.
